talking_points.headline: HSBC readies 'deep, wide and brutal' UK wealth cuts — up to 70% of advisers — as AI takes the servicing load
talking_points.context_html: HSBC is reportedly preparing to cut up to 70% of financial adviser roles in its UK wealth business, reversing a post-2021 hiring spree, as AI and digital servicing absorb more of the high-net-worth client journey. The plan is being read inside the bank as the first unambiguous bet that AI can carry core RM workload at scale. For Adam, this lands directly on his desk as the change-execution precedent: the APAC PB&WS platform, RM-workbench and Wealth-Intelligence investments will increasingly be judged against exactly this kind of AI-led servicing economics — and against the political cost of getting the human transition wrong.
source_links: Finextra: HSBC UK wealth cuts in AI push
Forbes: cuts even as investors want human judgment

talking_points.headline: Tokenised settlement hardens: HSBC, DBS, StanChart and Citi go live on Swift's ledger — but Taurus says key layers are still missing
talking_points.context_html: HSBC, Standard Chartered, DBS and Citi have completed live transactions on Swift's shared blockchain ledger, settling in minutes including on weekends, while Taurus' co-founder warns the network still lacks the internal layers needed for scaled production. The trials come on top of OCBC's tokenised-deposit firsts and HSBC's own Orion and RedCoin moves, so tokenised money is quietly becoming a production-rail question rather than a pilot question. For Adam, the near-term issue is readiness: WPB product and payments roadmaps will be expected to interoperate with these rails, and the build-vs-connect choices on his plate age quickly in this environment.
source_links: CoinDesk: Swift ledger needs key internal layers

talking_points.headline: On Adam's desk: DBS rolls Avaloq out across Asia with a S$1tn-by-2030 AUM target — the platform vendor HSBC runs on becomes a competitor weapon
talking_points.context_html: Following the DBS–Avaloq alliance deepening we covered on 6 October, DBS is now rolling Avaloq wealth software out across Asia as it extends the 18-year partnership, explicitly targeting S$1 trillion of assets under management by 2030. A direct competitor is turning HSBC's own core-banking vendor into a co-built distribution weapon, with a dated AUM ambition attached. For Adam's Avaloq 6.1 and credit-engine roadmap, DBS's rollout pace and delivery economics are the live external benchmark his stakeholders will quote back at him.

On Adam's Desk.title: DBS deepens Asia wealth push as DBS and Avaloq expand their 18-year alliance
On Adam's Desk.summary: DBS is rolling out Avaloq wealth software across Asia as it extends its 18-year vendor alliance, targeting S$1 trillion of assets under management by 2030. The update follows the alliance-deepening announcement covered earlier this week. Adam runs change execution on the same vendor platform, so DBS's rollout pace and its S$1tn ambition directly sharpen the competitive benchmark for his own Avaloq roadmap.

HSBC News.title: HSBC to make 'deep, wide and brutal' UK wealth management job cuts in AI push
HSBC News.summary: HSBC is planning to cut up to 70% of financial adviser roles in its UK wealth business as it ramps AI and digital servicing for high-net-worth clients, the FT reported. The move reverses a post-2021 hiring spree that brought hundreds of advisers into the UK franchise. For Adam it is the sharpest signal yet that the industry thinks AI can absorb core RM workload — the exact change-execution question his APAC platform work is racing to answer.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Swift blockchain ledger requires key internal layers, Taurus co-founder warns
Regulatory & Markets.summary: HSBC, Standard Chartered, DBS and Citi have completed live transactions on Swift's shared blockchain ledger, settling payments in minutes including on weekends, but Taurus' co-founder warns the network still needs key internal layers before scaled production use. The trials extend the tokenised-deposit work already running across the region. For Adam, tokenised settlement is shifting from pilot theatre to production plumbing on the vendor rails WPB's product roadmap will have to interoperate with.

Competitor Intelligence.title: OCBC launches tokenised deposit solution with Ant International for Singapore-Malaysia treasury
Competitor Intelligence.summary: OCBC is the first bank live on Ant International's WhaleRTP platform, letting the group move SGD and USD tokenised deposits 24/7 between Singapore and Malaysia with near-real-time settlement. Carmen Chan, Deputy Head of Global Transaction Banking at OCBC, called it tokenisation moving beyond experimentation, while Kelvin Li, General Manager of Platform Tech at Ant International, framed it as scalable adoption. It builds on OCBC's September cross-border tokenised deposit tests on Swift's ledger with Citi.

Operations & Change.title: Hyperlayer joins Asia Pacific fintech lab as finalist
Operations & Change.summary: Hyperlayer, founded by former Morgan Stanley executives Rob Rooney and Paul Rolles, joined an APAC fintech lab whose backers include HSBC, JP Morgan, Standard Chartered, UBS, Citi, DBS, OCBC and Hang Seng. Its pitch is letting banks ship product change without full core replacement — connecting multiple cores, in-house and vendor, at once. For Adam's core-banking change agenda, it is a live data point that 'wrap and extend' is attracting Tier-1 sponsorship as an alternative to big-bang migration.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Singapore's private banking client assets grew 15% in 2025, ~50% over five years
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Singapore's wealth management sector continues to grow, with private banking client assets up 15% last year and around 50% over five years, per Alvin Tan, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and MAS board member, citing Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong's remarks at the WMI Global-Asia Family Office Summit. MAS separately said it will trial tokenised MAS Bills settled in wholesale CBDC this year. The numbers reinforce why Singapore stays the region's deepest wealth battleground.

AI & Technology.title: Aveni CEO: why small AI models matter to UK finance
AI & Technology.summary: Joseph Twigg, CEO of Aveni, argued that smaller specialist models are becoming a practical priority for UK financial firms because they cost less to run, suit compliance work and reduce dependence on a few US providers — citing its 1-24 billion parameter FinLLM range co-developed with Lloyds Banking Group and Nationwide. He warned that hyperscaler disintermediation could turn banks into mere manufacturers if customers interact with their finances through ChatGPT or Anthropic. The 'requisite intelligence' framing is a useful counterweight to bigger-is-better model lobbying.
